[i][u]Current State of the Kaaganikan Revolution[/u][/i]
[spoiler]
After Admiral Tazi took control of the government with the help of his loyal officers and followers, he needed time to set up a new constitution for the socialist regime. All the while, revolts were occurring all across the nation in the chaos of it all, with most notable a strong Islamic rebel group in the south east, seeking either independence, a democratic Kaaganika, or integration into Baladullah.

Initially, there was also rebellions in the north, hoping for the return of the old regime. However, the old government was incredibly unpopular with the majority of the populace, with most seeing it as a corrupt entity, only there to steal what little money they had for themselves. These revolts quickly died down however, thanks to a surprisingly fast military kickback from the initial coup managing to destroy most hope for political normalcy in the nation.

Despite their ethnic and mild cultural differences, the Anikans and the Kaagans had surprisingly stayed mostly united in cause, not hoping for the complete collapse of the country for the sake of those not in the fight. The revolution had mostly consisted of slugfests between Islamic rebel groups and Kaaganikan armed forces, with the Kaaganikan Air Force being mild at best and the Navy, previously under command of Tazi, was actually pretty competent in their orders, being used for bombing raids on towns and villages under Islamic control.

During a particularly brutal battle at Djellal, Tazi had ordered essentially a kamikaze of the flagship of the navy, the KMNV Tetouan, a heavy cruiser loaded with thousands of pounds of explosives, sailed down the harbor before being evacuated, letting it ram into a nearby port and set off, completely leveling the harbor, and with it, the ship.

The Kaaganikans used this attack as justification for the destruction of the Islamic rebels, even after it was proven to be staged by the military. Some are questioning whether it was worth sacrificing the cruiser for at the very least until the end of the war, however it may end.
